rows.evidence: The anchor CN 21255955 (2020) keys 18 lots with a numbering that skips 2 (LOT-2 prints 3 'Produits surgelés', LOT-3 prints 4 …). Later notices of the chain use two interleaved schemes: 21923843 / 22230490 / 22219592 insert 'boissons' as 2 (LOT-2 prints 2, LOT-3 prints 3 'produits surgelés' …); 21923794 / 22231117 / 22654705 / 22958413 / 23435716 keep the anchor's numbering on LOT-1..LOT-11 (LOT-2 prints 3) and the 2021 'circuit court' numbers from LOT-12 on. K1 refused 21923794, 21923843, 22231117, 22219592 and 23435716 (pre-570 positional merge), which re-keyed the CARRIED numbers to the boissons scheme by v7. 570 then remapped 22654705 (v8) and 22958413 (v9) by printed number onto the carried keys: e.g. 'produits surgelés' (3) LOT-2 -> LOT-3, where the carried lot (22219592's LOT-3) prints 3 'produits surgelés - circuit traditionnel' (agree), but where the ANCHOR's lot is 'Produits laitiers et ovo-produits' (disagree); the anchor's 'Produits surgelés' is at LOT-2, i.e. the section's own key. So the move agrees with the lot it joins and with 570's rule (targets = carried numbers; parity holds), and disagrees with the anchor reference the 570 measurement used for its 124/124 title evidence. Every notice prints surgelés = 3, so the printed number is consistent across the chain; the key identity is not. Impact: 0 award blocks moved (all 8 served results lot null, before and after); the served head equals the remap-off head (the last notice 23435716 is K1-refused, keeps its own keys and supersedes all 23 keys); only versions 8 and 9 carry different lot content. Per-key number changes across the 10 versions: 75 with the remap, 82 without. Shape: a weld of yearly re-tenders of one buyer (2020-2023) with two lot numbering schemes (issue 364's class), seen 0 times in 570's 211 replayed chains.
